items.hook: Ancient Red Dragon is perfect for a playful encounter that can still punish bad habits.
items.body: With an Armor Class of 22 and 507 hit points, the Ancient Red Dragon presents a formidable challenge. Its commanding presence can disrupt party coordination, while its fiery breath weapon deals 26d6 fire damage in a 90-foot cone. Underestimating the dragon's 80-foot fly speed allows it to dictate engagement range, making it crucial to use terrain to limit its movement options. Forcing the dragon into predictable attack patterns can mitigate its battlefield control.
items.cta: DMs: Use a cliff or cavern ceiling to negate the dragon's 80-foot fly speed advantage and limit its fiery breath.

items.hook: The Order of Combat dictates that initiative determines turn sequence, not speed or dexterity.
items.body: Initiative, not dexterity modifiers or movement speed, decides who acts first in combat. Conflating dexterity with initiative leads to confusion when slower characters act before faster ones. This misunderstanding can disrupt strategy and timing. Planning actions based on actual turn order, determined by initiative rolls, prevents misplaced assumptions about character speed.
items.cta: DMs: Remind your players that page 13 clearly states initiative order dictates combat turns, not dexterity or speed.

items.hook: Wizard spells scale dramatically at level 5 with access to 3rd-level spells.
items.body: A Wizard's power spike occurs at level 5 when 3rd-level spells become available. Many players underestimate the impact of spells like Fireball, which deals 8d6 damage in a 20-foot radius. Mismanagement occurs when players rely on low-level spells or cantrips instead of utilizing these more potent options. Optimal play involves planning spell slots and positioning to maximize area effects and manage resources effectively.
items.cta: DMs: Remind your Wizards that at level 5, 8d6 Fireball beats cantrips, so they should stop hoarding spell slots.

items.hook: Low-threat on paper, high-chaos at the table: Bugbear Stalker.
items.body: AC 15 and HP 65 mean it can take a few hits while executing its plan. With a Stealth bonus of +6, it often surprises parties, making the first move count. Abduct allows it to reposition enemies easily, disrupting formations. Ignoring this mobility can lead to disastrous positioning errors. Focus fire on the Bugbear Stalker to prevent it from dictating the battle's flow.
items.cta: Players: laugh first, then respect turn economy before this joke encounter snowballs.

items.hook: Word of Radiance is the spell people joke about - right before it saves a turn cycle.
items.body: Word of Radiance is a cantrip that deals 1d6 radiant damage and requires a Constitution saving throw. It targets all chosen creatures within a 5-foot sphere, not just one. Casting it against high-Constitution enemies often results in failed damage rolls. Better results occur when used against multiple low-Constitution targets clustered around the caster, increasing the likelihood of successful damage application.
items.cta: DMs: When you're surrounded by weaklings, unleash Word of Radiance to exploit their low Constitution and clear the rabble.

items.hook: Two-Weapon Fighting reduces attack dice size based on Agility.
items.body: With Two-Weapon Fighting, both attacks use smaller dice along the dice chain, directly affecting combat effectiveness. High Agility minimizes this penalty, making dual-wielding viable. Low Agility means the penalty outweighs the benefit, leading to inefficient combat choices. Recognizing the dice chain interaction is crucial for effective use.
items.cta: Judges: If their Agility isn't high enough, remind them they're just swinging two butter knives with worse odds.

items.hook: Oath of Glory paladins pivot roles between setup and closer based on party needs.
items.body: Channel Divinity options allow Oath of Glory paladins to either bolster allies or strike decisively. Overcommitting to one role can leave the party unbalanced, especially in dynamic encounters. Alternating between enhancing allies and dealing damage ensures consistent impact. This subclass excels by adapting to the flow of combat, maintaining effectiveness across different phases.
items.cta: DMs: Remind your Oath of Glory paladin to use Channel Divinity tactically, alternating between ally support and enemy takedown as needed.

items.hook: Backstab grants extra weapon dice when hitting an unaware target.
items.body: Backstab triggers when a thief hits a creature unaware of the attack, dealing an extra weapon die of damage plus additional weapon dice equal to half the thief's level, rounded down. Declaring the trigger before rolling is crucial to ensure the bonus applies without dispute. This prevents invalidating the bonus due to oversight.
items.cta: GMs: Have the thief declare Backstab before rolling to ensure they get the extra damage dice without argument.

items.hook: Two-Weapon Fighting reduces attack dice size based on Agility.
items.body: Two-Weapon Fighting allows characters to attack with both a primary weapon and a light off-hand weapon in the same round. Both attacks use smaller dice along the dice chain, with penalties decreasing as Agility increases. Low Agility results in inefficient dual-wielding due to increased penalties. High Agility minimizes penalties and maximizes attack effectiveness, making dual-wielding more viable.
items.cta: Judges: If their Agility is below 16, remind them they're just flailing with those smaller dice.

items.hook: Oath of Glory allows paladins to shift roles between setup and closer effectively.
items.body: Channel Divinity: Peerless Athlete grants advantage on Strength and Dexterity checks for 10 minutes, but players often waste it on minor tasks. The real value comes from using it to set up for a decisive combat or skill challenge. Inspiring Smite lets you distribute temporary hit points after a successful attack, yet many forget to use it as a buffer against incoming damage. The key is to toggle between these abilities to maintain momentum and avoid overcommitting to a single strategy.
items.cta: DMs: Have your Oath of Glory paladin use Peerless Athlete for crucial Strength checks, not trivial tasks, to control the encounter's pace.

items.hook: Backstab adds weapon dice based on thief level when the target is unaware.
items.body: Backstab requires the attacker to call the trigger and apply the effect once per attack. Thieves add an extra weapon die of damage on a hit against an unaware creature, plus additional weapon dice equal to half the thief's level, rounded down. Declaring the trigger consistently avoids disputes. Clear rulings now save argument time later.
items.cta: GMs: Make the thief declare their Backstab before rolling; they add one weapon die per two levels when unnoticed.

items.hook: Scrolls of the Forbidden Summoning compel a Will DC 13 check to avoid completing the ritual.
items.body: Summoning a Demon Type II or III without a spell check sounds tempting until you realize the demon arrives unbound and hostile. Casters who fail the Will DC 13 check are forced to finish the ritual, with the DC increasing to 16 for chaotic readers. The scroll's one-time use means it crumbles to ash after reading, leaving no room for second attempts. Prioritize positioning and containment strategies before activating this volatile item.
items.cta: Judges: Only let them touch the Scrolls of the Forbidden Summoning when they've got a DC 13 Will save strategy ready.

items.hook: Vulture is the classic 'easy fight' that gets weird fast if players autopilot.
items.body: With an Armor Class of 10 and only 5 hit points, the Vulture relies on Pack Tactics to offset its fragility. Its Beak attack becomes significantly more threatening with Advantage, allowing it to swarm a target effectively. Misjudging its low challenge rating can lead to underestimating the tactical edge Pack Tactics provides. Disrupting the Vulture's adjacency forces it to break formation, negating its Advantage.
items.cta: DMs: run it with a wink, then punish lazy positioning once so the lesson lands.

items.hook: Spidersilk only works while you maintain focus.
items.body: Spidersilk's duration is Focus, meaning any distraction breaks it. Common misplay: casting it to show off, not to solve a problem. Better play: use it to bypass obstacles or gain tactical advantage, ensuring it directly impacts the encounter's outcome.
items.cta: GMs: Enforce Spidersilk's Focus duration; any distraction ends it, so remind them to stay sharp or fall.

items.hook: Scrolls of the Forbidden Summoning compel a Will DC 13 check or force the caster to complete the ritual.
items.body: The scrolls summon a Demon Type II or III without a spell check, but the demon is immediately hostile and unbound. Chaotic readers face a higher compulsion DC of 16. Immediate hostility and lack of control often lead to disastrous positioning. Preparing containment measures before reading the scroll mitigates the risk.
items.cta: Judges: Only use the Scrolls of the Forbidden Summoning if the party has a solid plan for an unbound, hostile demon.

items.hook: Vulture is the classic 'easy fight' that gets weird fast if players autopilot.
items.body: With an Armor Class of 10 and 5 hit points, Vulture relies on Pack Tactics to gain advantage on attack rolls. Adjacent allies are required to trigger this, and its walking speed of 10 feet limits repositioning. Engaging Vulture in isolation prevents it from gaining advantage. Use movement to disrupt its adjacency and deny it advantage.
items.cta: DMs: run it with a wink, then punish lazy positioning once so the lesson lands.

items.hook: Spidersilk's duration is Focus, not a set time limit.
items.body: Casting Spidersilk without a plan wastes its potential, as it requires Focus to maintain. The common mistake: using it just because it's available, rather than for strategic movement or combat advantage. Optimal use involves timing it to force enemy movement, disrupt their actions, or expedite combat resolution.
items.cta: GMs: Demand players state their intent and target before casting Spidersilk, as its Focus duration demands strategic precision.

items.hook: Light tone, real consequences: build the scene around Cacophony Golem and table overconfidence.
items.body: Magic missiles from a Cacophony Golem deal 1d4+1 damage and require a DC 13 Reflex save to avoid, with a range of 100 feet. Its movement is 0', meaning it remains stationary unless forced to move by external means. The golem's ability to induce insanity adds pressure, but the real threat comes from its cacophony ability, which often goes untelegraphed. Engaging from a distance and leveraging non-magical attacks bypasses its spell resistance, turning the encounter into a battle of attrition.
items.cta: Judges: Remind them that spells have a 50% failure rate and the golem's 0' movement makes it a sitting duck for arrows.

items.hook: Investiture of Flame grants immunity to fire damage and resistance to cold damage for up to 10 minutes.
items.body: Investiture of Flame requires concentration, meaning it competes with other concentration spells and can be disrupted by damage. Many players mistakenly use it solely for its 1d10 fire damage, overlooking its potential to shift the action economy by neutralizing fire-based threats. The optimal play involves using it to change the battlefield dynamics, such as negating enemy fire attacks, rather than just adding another damage source.
items.cta: DMs: Use Investiture of Flame when fire immunity will nullify an enemy's main attack, not just for the 1d10 damage.

items.hook: Halflings have the best Luck economy in the game.
items.body: Halflings use Good Fortune once per session, adding their Luck die to any roll, or granting it to a nearby ally, without burning Luck. This mechanic is often misused for high-stakes rolls when it shines in consistent, repeatable actions. With +4 AC against large foes and superior stealth, Halflings excel in avoiding damage and maintaining position.
items.cta: Judges: Remind your Halfling to use their Luck die for stealth checks; it's the consistent edge they keep forgetting.

items.hook: Unseen Attackers and Targets impose Disadvantage on attack rolls against unseen targets.
items.body: When attacking a target you can't see, you always have Disadvantage on the attack roll, regardless of whether you guess the target's location or hear it. This rule often gets misapplied when players assume sound negates the Disadvantage. Correct application involves understanding that Disadvantage applies until the target is visible, ensuring clear rulings and reducing disputes.
items.cta: DMs: Enforce Disadvantage on attacks against unseen targets until visibility is restored; hearing alone doesn't cut it.

items.hook: Yes, Assassin looks harmless - until the table underestimates it and gives it free turns.
items.body: Assassin's Execute talent multiplies damage by three against surprised targets, making initial positioning and awareness critical. The +6 attack bonus and 2d4 poisoned dagger damage become devastating when surprise is achieved. Focusing solely on damage without securing position first often results in costly mistakes. Controlling movement lanes and isolating targets can neutralize the Assassin's advantage.
items.cta: DMs: run it with a wink, then punish lazy positioning once so the lesson lands.

items.hook: Two-Weapon Fighting uses smaller dice along the dice chain with both weapons.
items.body: Two-Weapon Fighting requires high Agility to mitigate penalties. Characters with low Agility suffer from reduced effectiveness due to the smaller dice used for both attacks. Many players overlook that dual-wielding without sufficient Agility is a losing proposition. Optimal play involves ensuring high Agility to minimize penalties and maximize attack potential.
items.cta: Judges: Remind them that without 13+ Agility, their two-weapon dreams are just a dice chain downgrade.

items.hook: Barrier Tattoo only works without armor.
items.body: Barrier Tattoo requires attunement and provides an AC bonus based on rarity: +1 for uncommon, +2 for rare, +3 for very rare. Wearing armor negates its effect, as it only functions without armor. Its application demands an anchor point and space, making it impractical in cramped spaces or mid-combat.
items.cta: DMs: Remind players that Barrier Tattoo's AC bonus is void if they wear armor; plan attunement logistics before combat.

items.hook: Spell Casting Check consumes the slot on failure.
items.body: Roll d20 plus the relevant stat modifier against DC 10 plus the spell tier to cast a spell. Failure means the spell doesn't activate, but the slot is still consumed. A critical failure for Wizards triggers a mishap. Rushed rolls without confirming the DC lead to unnecessary slot loss. Confirming the DC before rolling prevents this common error.
items.cta: GMs: Ensure players calculate DC as 10 plus spell tier before rolling to prevent unnecessary spell slot loss.

items.hook: Mechanics moment: Saving Throws and Damage.
items.body: Quick example for Saving Throws and Damage: call the trigger, then apply the effect once. Damage dealt via saving throws uses these rules. ## Damage against Multiple Targets When you create a damaging effect that forces two or more targets to make saving throws against it at the same time. Clear rulings now save argument time later.
items.cta: DMs: Run a quick example of saving throws and damage with multiple targets to set tonight's precedent.

items.hook: Use Mastiff as 'comic relief' that quietly pressures the party's decisions.
items.body: With a bite attack of 1d6 damage and a +1 to hit, the Mastiff's offensive potential is limited. Its movement range is 'near', which can be easily miscalculated in the heat of battle. Neglecting the importance of positioning and timing leads to wasted actions when the Mastiff can't reach its target. Using the Mastiff as a distraction or for objectives that don't require sustained combat presence is more effective.
items.cta: GMs: Track the Mastiff's 'near' movement closely; misjudging distance wastes its 1d6 bite in time-sensitive encounters.

items.hook: Disapproval (Cleric Mechanic) increases with each failed spell check.
items.body: Disapproval starts by triggering only on a natural 1, but each failed cleric spell check expands the range by 1 for the day. Clerics who ignore this cumulative effect and cast spells recklessly face greater risk of triggering disapproval. Managing spell casting judiciously and resetting disapproval through rest, prayer, or acts of faith before it becomes a significant risk is crucial.
items.cta: Judges: Enforce disapproval range increases with each failed spell check; clerics must rest or pray to reset it.

items.hook: Fey Wanderer: Dreadful Strikes deals 1d4 psychic damage once per turn.
items.body: Dreadful Strikes allows a Fey Wanderer to deal 1d4 psychic damage once per turn on a hit with a weapon, and it doesn't stack with Hunter's Mark. Combining features that don't synergize dilutes impact. Consistent damage output comes from focusing on repeatable actions rather than stacking effects.
items.cta: DMs: Remind your Fey Wanderer to choose subclass features that prioritize consistent 1d4 psychic damage over redundant effects like Hunter's Mark.

items.hook: Hard lesson: Torch and Light.
items.body: Myth vs rule: Torch and Light. Torches last 1 hour of real time. Characters without darkvision must carry a light source or be blind. Tracking real time is core to Shadowdark play. Clear rulings now save argument time later.
items.cta: GMs: Set a timer for each torch; when it hits 60 minutes, remind them they're in the dark.

items.hook: The Sword of Air and Darkness transports targets to the ethereal plane on a natural 19-20.
items.body: The +2 bonus to attack and damage is straightforward, but the ethereal plane effect is often mishandled. Players frequently overlook the importance of the 1d6 round duration, failing to capitalize on the temporary removal of a foe. The darkness spell, cast once per day at a result of 18, should be used strategically to control the battlefield. The curse's Will DC 12 check each night risks permanent Luck loss, often ignored until it's too late.
items.cta: Judges: When they roll a natural 19-20, remind them to exploit the 1d6 rounds of ethereal isolation.

items.hook: Gold Dragon Wyrmling is the classic 'easy fight' that gets weird fast if players autopilot.
items.body: Fire Breath has a recharge of 5-6 and deals 15 (4d6) fire damage in a 15-foot cone, with a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. Its flying speed of 60 feet allows it to reposition easily, making it hard to pin down. Amphibious nature means it can engage in both air and underwater combat without penalty. Spreading out denies its ability to use Fire Breath effectively, and preventing it from leveraging its flight to isolate targets is crucial.
items.cta: Players: laugh first, then respect turn economy before this joke encounter snowballs.

items.hook: Magic Circle requires Focus to maintain.
items.body: Magic Circle creates a near-sized cube centered on the caster, preventing a named creature type from attacking or casting hostile spells for as long as Focus is maintained. Breaking Focus ends the protection immediately, leaving the caster vulnerable. Ensure the caster remains undisturbed to leverage the circle for strategic positioning or negotiation without interruption.
items.cta: GMs: Keep the caster's Focus uninterrupted; one slip and that Magic Circle's gone, leaving them wide open.

items.hook: Laulich is perfect for a playful encounter that can still punish bad habits.
items.body: The magic suppression field prevents all spellcasting within 60 feet, nullifying spells regardless of caster level or spell type. Casting spells within this range results in wasted actions. Engaging Laulich from outside the field's range or using non-magical tactics is more effective. Laulich's madness gaze (2/day) requires a Will save, with failure causing confusion for 1d4 rounds, often disrupting coordinated plans.
items.cta: Judges: Force the players to exploit the terrain to stay beyond Laulich's 60-foot magic suppression field or waste their spells.

items.hook: Heal restores 70 Hit Points and ends Blinded, Deafened, and Poisoned conditions instantly.
items.body: Casting Heal requires an action and targets one creature within 60 feet. The common error is casting it reactively without considering its full potential impact. Heal's utility extends beyond hit point restoration; it can remove debilitating conditions that might otherwise cost multiple actions to address. Optimal play involves timing its use to negate these conditions at a critical moment, potentially altering the course of combat.
items.cta: DMs: Use Heal when 70 hit points and condition removal can prevent your party from wasting multiple actions on recovery.

items.hook: The Witch's Familiar allows spells to originate from its location, not yours.
items.body: With 1d4 hit dice and leather armor, the Witch is fragile and must avoid frontline combat. The Familiar can be revived by sacrificing 1d4 HP, which is often underestimated as a strategic resource. Players commonly misuse the Familiar by keeping it too close, negating its utility as a remote spell source. Position the Familiar strategically to maximize spell range and maintain distance from threats.
items.cta: GMs: Remind players the Familiar's range is their spell range; keep it out of harm's way for maximum utility.

items.hook: Playing on a Grid means each square represents 5 feet.
items.body: The common mistake when Playing on a Grid is prioritizing speed over clarity, leading to misinterpretations of movement. Each square on the grid equals 5 feet, and movement should be calculated square by square, not foot by foot. This prevents disputes over distances and ensures consistent rulings. Clear rulings now prevent arguments later.
items.cta: DMs: Enforce 5-foot square movement to avoid disputes and keep your game from devolving into a geometry lesson.

items.hook: Healing restores 1 HP per night while adventuring, 2 HP with full bed rest.
items.body: Wounds mend with rest but never exceed the natural maximum. Critical-hit effects, like a speed penalty from a wounded kneecap, heal only when their associated damage heals. Assuming critical effects heal independently leads to persistent penalties. Ensuring damage is fully healed avoids lingering effects.
items.cta: Judges: Remind them that ignoring bed rest means dragging that bum knee through every encounter until it's fully healed.

items.hook: Weapon of Warning (Rapier): humble gear with main-character energy when the table gets creative.
items.body: The Weapon of Warning (Rapier) wakes allies from natural sleep when combat starts but not from magical sleep. Its range for granting Advantage on Initiative is 30 feet, which requires precise positioning. Keeping allies within this range before combat ensures they benefit from the bonus. Use this to secure a tactical position before hostilities begin.
items.cta: DMs: Position the party within 30 feet of the Weapon of Warning (Rapier) to ensure Advantage on Initiative rolls.

items.hook: Difficulty Class determines success or failure with a single roll.
items.body: Difficulty Class: Easy DC 9, Normal DC 12, Hard DC 15, Extreme DC 18. Characters roll d20 plus relevant stat modifier against the DC. Misjudging intent before rolling leads to unnecessary disputes. Establishing intent, trigger, and outcome before rolling ensures clarity and expedites resolution.
items.cta: GMs: Establish intent, trigger, and outcome before rolling against DC 12 to avoid pointless arguments.

items.hook: Yes, Kaundyuk looks harmless - until the table underestimates it and gives it free turns.
items.body: With a bite attack at +8 dealing 1d8 damage plus poison and two claw attacks at +8 for 1d8+2 each, Kaundyuk can inflict significant damage if left unchecked. Its critical range of 19-20 with a DN/d6 crit die increases the odds of high-impact hits. Focusing on its 6d12 hit dice misses the real danger: the ability to consistently land multiple high-damage attacks. Disrupting its action economy immediately is more effective than attempting to outlast its barrage.
items.cta: Players: laugh first, then respect turn economy before this joke encounter snowballs.

items.hook: Light tone, real consequences: build the scene around Adult Blue Dragon and table overconfidence.
items.body: Lightning Breath deals 66 (12d10) lightning damage in a 90-foot line; it recharges on a roll of 5-6. Underestimating the dragon's 80-foot fly speed combined with its 40-foot burrow speed leads to poor positioning and wasted actions. Assuming the dragon will stay grounded or visible results in tactical errors. Using terrain to limit its mobility and force it into disadvantageous positions is crucial.
items.cta: DMs: Use the dragon's 80-foot fly speed to exploit players' poor positioning; force them to respect its mobility or suffer.

items.hook: The Necklace Of Charm sets your Charisma stat to 18 (+4) while worn.
items.body: The Necklace Of Charm overrides your Charisma to 18, replacing any existing bonuses or penalties. This means characters with high Charisma gain no benefit, as their stat is effectively capped. Giving this to the character with the lowest Charisma optimizes the party's overall effectiveness.
items.cta: GMs: Hand the Necklace Of Charm to the party's charisma-challenged member; their Charisma becomes 18, no questions asked.

items.hook: Fly drops you mid-air if the spell ends unexpectedly.
items.body: Fly is a 3rd-level wizard spell with a range of self or touch, and its duration is determined by the spell check result. Misjudging the duration and speed can lead to abrupt falls when the spell ends. Half speed applies when climbing, double when diving, and it's halved if heavily loaded. Cast Fly when the risk of falling is minimal, such as near the ground or with a backup plan in place.
items.cta: Judges: Remind them Fly's spell check determines duration - cast it low to the ground unless they enjoy plummeting.

items.hook: Hiding requires the DM to determine when circumstances allow it.
items.body: Hiding depends on environmental conditions and DM discretion, not just a Stealth check. Many assume hiding is always an option, overlooking line of sight and cover requirements. Clear communication from the DM on visibility and obstructions is essential to avoid disputes. Consistency in rulings maintains game flow and player understanding.
items.cta: DMs: Clarify that hiding requires both cover and a successful Stealth check, not just a whim or wish.

items.hook: Kraken is perfect for a playful encounter that can still punish bad habits.
items.body: The Kraken's storm effect creates violently turbulent seas in a 1-mile radius for 2d4 rounds. Ignoring the risk of capsizing can lead to disastrous consequences when the ship capsizes mid-combat. Preparing for potential capsizing or avoiding the storm entirely is critical when engaging the Kraken.
items.cta: GMs: Make them roll a DEX save DC 15 each round or watch their ship capsize in the Kraken's storm.

items.hook: Mighty Deeds of Arms require no saving throw or opposed roll.
items.body: Mighty Deeds of Arms allow Warriors and Dwarves to declare a Deed before attacking, such as tripping or disarming, which succeeds if the attack hits and the Deed die shows 3 or higher. The Deed die, which scales from d3 to d10+, determines the Deed's effectiveness. Many assume an opposed roll or saving throw is needed, but none is required. Consistent rulings on Deed declarations streamline gameplay and avoid disputes.
items.cta: Judges: Enforce that Mighty Deeds need no saving throw; just a hit and a Deed die of 3 or more.

items.hook: Path of Wild Magic triggers random magical effects while raging.
items.body: Magic Awareness at 3rd level allows detection of spells or magic items within 60 feet as an action, limited by proficiency bonus uses per long rest. Attempting detection in combat wastes an action when actions are limited. Use it during exploration to gather information without sacrificing combat efficiency. Role pivoting requires clear communication to prevent over-investment in setup or finishing moves.
items.cta: DMs: Signal the Path of Wild Magic pivot by declaring your action economy shift from Magic Awareness to rage-induced chaos.

items.hook: Morale checks trigger at half losses or when a strong ally falls.
items.body: Monsters make a morale check with DC 15 Wisdom when half their number are defeated or a powerful ally falls. Failure results in fleeing or surrendering. Skipping this step leads to unnecessary debates. Enforce it consistently to keep the game moving.
items.cta: GMs: Roll a DC 15 Wisdom check for morale at half losses or a fallen ally; skip it and expect chaos.

items.hook: Boots of Mist-Stepping allow movement through 30 feet of air as mist, once per day.
items.body: The effect lasts 1 round and requires materializing in an unoccupied space. Players frequently misuse this by activating it without clear destination, risking wasted turns. The practical application is using it to bypass obstacles or reposition strategically before engagement, not during it. Misuse leads to unnecessary exposure and damage from failed Fortitude saves (DC 11) causing 1d3 damage over 1d4 rounds.
items.cta: Judges: Have them use the Boots of Mist-Stepping to bypass obstacles pre-combat, avoiding the Fort DC 11 curse mid-battle.

items.hook: Awakened Tree has a Strength score of 19 and a Slam attack that deals 3d6 + 4 bludgeoning damage.
items.body: With an Armor Class of 13 and 59 hit points, the Awakened Tree withstands attacks from low-level parties. Its 20-foot movement speed limits its mobility, but the Slam attack can force opponents to engage on its terms. Attempts to incapacitate it often fail due to its Constitution score of 15, which bolsters its saving throws against such effects. Exploiting its low Dexterity of 6 can limit its effectiveness through area control spells.
items.cta: DMs: Place the Awakened Tree in dense forest terrain to mitigate its 20-foot speed and maximize its 3d6 + 4 Slam attack.

items.hook: Passwall creates a temporary tunnel for 5 rounds in a barrier you touch.
items.body: Passwall's range is Close, and it lasts for 5 rounds, allowing a tunnel of your height in a straight line up to near distance. Casting Passwall strictly for combat positioning within the grid misses its potential for bypassing obstacles or accessing hidden areas. Casting it to gain strategic information or access can influence the environment beyond mere movement.
items.cta: GMs: Force them to use Passwall's 5-round window to bypass obstacles, not just shuffle around the grid.
